title: SCRIBE v3: Three Count-Based Judges of Generated Text
description: SCRIBE is a metric for generated text built from counts alone, with no neural network. Version 1.0 described SCRIBE v2, which reads about twenty statistics of a text against human reference text and passes a control ladder of degraded text where standard per-text metrics fail. This version adds two judges of other kinds. SURPRISE reads the text's code length word by word under a count model of the pack (a Kneser–Ney trigram with spelling models, a cache and a match model), two-sided, so text more predictable than human text loses as surely as salad. MATCH reads matching statistics against a suffix array of the pack, the text's Lempel–Ziv complexity and echo of a prompt. Neither uses word vectors or co-occurrence. They were built because a writer, K5, gained +0.145 on v2 from a sentence gate that picks sentences by word co-occurrence with the prompt, while v2's coherence axis also rests on co-occurrence. The new judges do not confirm that gain (SURPRISE −0.106) or a later gain from more training text. SCRIBE v3, the plain mean of v2, SURPRISE and MATCH, passed its fresh control ladder but caught only 5 of 9 registered attacks, because one judge's catch was diluted. SCRIBE v3.1, the recommended form, is the geometric mean of v2 and new versions of the judges that add statistics for words that fit neither neighbour and for bland text. On two fresh Wikipedia regions it passes all five ladder pairs (0.966–0.968 on the hardest) and all 9 registered attacks (v2: 5), catching copied prompt sentences, keyword stuffing at one word in five or more, and generic paragraphs. It ranks human web text above every GPT-2 top-k system (Spearman +0.90; v2 −0.70), fixing v2's "too typical" blind spot in the mean, and it sees relevance to a story prompt (HANNA Kendall 0.169; v2 0.017). It scores about 590 texts per second on one CPU core. It is not fool-proof: it passes only 2 and 3 of 8 held-out attacks; stuffing at one word in seven, a template with the prompt's names, a title swap and loosely related fluent sentences get through. Sentence order, truncated sentences and truth are invisible to all three judges; it does not rank models that all write salad, passes 3 of 5 pairs on novels and 4 of 5 on web text, cannot tell a right answer from another question's on Dolly, and needs 500 reference samples per bucket. Its agreement with people is about v2's. Of twenty predictions registered before this version's reads, twelve hit, five hit in part and three missed.
notes: Version 2.0 of this record (version 1.0, 28 October 2026, described SCRIBE v2). Three files: SCRIBE_paper.pdf (the paper, CC BY 4.0); SCRIBE_code_v2.0.zip (all code: the SCRIBE metric and tool in C++20 with profiles v1, v2, v3 and v3.1, the word-vector builder, the evaluation and run scripts, every version's freeze record, this version's registration with its predictions, and the paper source; GNU AGPL v3); SCRIBE_results_v2.0.zip (every result table of versions 2.0 and 1.0 as Markdown, CSV and JSON). No third-party text is redistributed; the code's data.py downloads and prepares every dataset.
